newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore meets on Waterford, decision unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore meets on Waterford, decision unlikely.

text.p: The board of Ireland's Avonmore Foods Plc will meet later today to discuss Waterford Foods Plc's rejection of its merger proposal but industry sources said Avonmore was unlikely to make a final decision on its next move.
Avonmore launched its 281 million Irish pound ($427.1 million) offer in early April in a bid to create Ireland's biggest food group and a major European player with turnover of 2.5 billion.
Analysts said the merged company would be a good fit and create substantial synergies and economies of scale.

But Waterford baulked at the proposal, which it said did not reflect its underlying value or strategic position. The cooperative's supplier farmers and workers feared any rationalisation could slash jobs.
A senior food industry source said on Monday that Avonmore's board was not expected to ditch its merger proposal at the meeting in Kilkenny, south-east Ireland.
"But it's unlikely that a major improvement to the bid could be made and I think it's reasonable to assume that a final decision would be unlikely today," the source said.

A spokesman for Avonmore confirmed the Waterford proposal was on the regular meeting's agenda. He said it was unclear how long the board would meet and said a statement, if one were issued, would come in the afternoon.
Despite Waterford's rejection of the offer, the company has said it agrees with the concept of merger or industry consolidation to boost shareholder value -- a statement welcomed by Avonmore.

Avonmore has been careful to portray the offer as a "friendly" merger, aware that it must be ratified by 75 percent of Waterford Co-op, which owns 68 percent of the Plc's shares, and Waterford Foods shareholders.

Avonmore says the food sector is facing enormous changes which could hit the incomes and livelihoods of Waterford's supplier farmers. It says further consolidation is needed in the Irish dairy industry and that the merger with Waterford would be in the best interests of shareholders and milk suppliers for both organisations.
Under the terms of the merger proposal, Avonmore has offered one Avonmore share for every two Waterfords Foods Plc and Waterford Co-op Ltd ordinary shares.
